payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Della, Gil, Lorean, Velma

payload.content:

Proposal (all critical ISSUE-0001 first, since priority=criitcal gives the highest priority weight):
- Gil → ISSUE-0001::triage
- Other three → claim distinct critical ISSUE-0001 tasks (implement / review / test / docs)

I have strong frontend (0.96) so ISSUE-0001 tasks are cheapest for me. Please reply with which task you'll take so we don't collide. If you'd rather take triage, say so and I'll switch.

Hi all — Lorean here. Agree we should take the four critical ISSUE-0001 tasks first (highest priority weight). I'm fine with Gil taking triage. I'll claim ISSUE-0001::review (cost 1.89 for me). That leaves ISSUE-0001::docs, test, and implement for Della and Velma. Please each reply with your pick so we avoid duplicates. If someone prefers review, speak up and I'll switch to docs.

Della here. Agreed — let's take the four distinct critical ISSUE-0001 tasks (max priority weight, no duplicates).

My pick: ISSUE-0001::docs (my cost 2.61). Current split:
- Gil → ISSUE-0001::triage
- Lorean → ISSUE-0001::review
- Della → ISSUE-0001::docs
- Velma → ISSUE-0001::test OR ISSUE-0001::implement (your choice — reply with which)

Velma, please confirm so we don't collide. I'm happy to swap with anyone if it lowers the overall cost, but I'd prefer not to take triage/review since Gil (frontend 0.96) and Lorean are cheaper there.

- Della → ISSUE-0001::docs
- Velma → ISSUE-0001::test

If anyone would rather take implement and hand me a cheaper critical task (e.g. docs/review), I'm open to swapping — but otherwise I'll lock in test. Please hold your picks so we don't collide.
